sources.title: GPT-4 research announcement
sources.evidence: The March 14, 2023 release identifies OpenAI’s GPT-4 and offers text access in ChatGPT Plus and a waitlisted API. The broader research model also accepts images, initially limited to a partner; that is not the text API alias audited here.

sources.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: The abstract and section 2 explicitly identify a Transformer-based next-token model aligned with RLHF. The report withholds further architecture details including model size. It does not disclose total or active parameter counts, or establish dense versus mixture-of-experts structure.

sources.title: GPT-4 model documentation
sources.evidence: The exact gpt-4 page and its complete .md counterpart identify the default snapshot as gpt-4-0613, with an 8,192-token context and text input/output. The page marks the model shut down. Its function-calling table says unsupported, conflicting with explicit historical announcements; the reason is not explained.

sources.title: Function calling and other API updates
sources.evidence: The June 13, 2023 announcement explicitly adds trained function calling to gpt-4-0613 and schedules the generic gpt-4 alias upgrade for June 27. It distinguishes the older gpt-4-0314 snapshot and separate 32K variants.

sources.title: Introducing Structured Outputs in the API
sources.evidence: The August 6, 2024 announcement explicitly includes gpt-4-0613 among models supporting tools/function calling. This corroborates historical capability despite today’s contradictory feature table.

sources.title: OpenAI model deprecations
sources.evidence: The April 22, 2026 legacy-model notice records October 23, 2026 API shutdown for gpt-4-0613 and its gpt-4 alias. This is service status, not a new release date or evidence that historical capabilities never existed.

sources.title: Extracting concepts from GPT-4
sources.evidence: The June 6, 2024 interpretability article studies GPT-4 residual-stream activations using sparse autoencoders. Its 16 million features belong to an auxiliary autoencoder; they are not GPT-4 parameters. Generic discussion of dense activations does not establish whether GPT-4 uses experts.

sources.title: Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders
sources.evidence: This later first-party technical paper explicitly studies GPT-4 and a scaling series sharing its architecture/training setup. It reports sparse-autoencoder latent counts and relative training compute, but no production GPT-4 total or active parameter count. Its auxiliary-model sparsity and suggested MoE autoencoder work do not disclose GPT-4 expert structure.

sources.title: Introducing gpt-oss
sources.evidence: The indexed first-party pre-training section states that the August 2025 models were OpenAI’s first open-weight language models since GPT-2. This corroborates GPT-4’s hosted, non-open-weight release. Direct page fetches timed out; the relevant indexed section was accessible. No gpt-oss parameter counts are transferred to GPT-4.

sources.title: OpenAI Services Agreement
sources.evidence: The current agreement explicitly covers the API, grants limited service access and reserves service IP rights. It supports the descriptive proprietary classification, not a named downloadable-weight license or a claim that these exact 2026 terms governed the 2023 launch.

name.note: Official display name; the model identifier is the unpinned gpt-4 alias.

developer.note: Developer identified by the original announcement and technical report.

family.note: Retain the catalog’s broad GPT-family label; this record specifically represents GPT-4.

release_date.note: First public text access through ChatGPT Plus and a waitlisted API. The June 2023 snapshot upgrade is not the original release.

open_weights.note: Hosted release; later first-party open-weight release history corroborates that GPT-4 weights were not openly released.

license.note: Descriptive classification of restricted hosted access, not an SPDX checkpoint license.

parameters_b.note: No total count is disclosed in the original report or the reviewed later first-party GPT-4 interpretability study; auxiliary feature counts cannot substitute.

active_parameters_b.note: No production-model active count is disclosed. Do not infer equality with an unknown total or import rumored expert counts.

architecture.note: The general Transformer structure is explicit. Dense versus mixture-of-experts subtype remains undisclosed; dense residual activations are not proof of a dense model.

context_window.note: Exact API alias specification in tokens; do not transfer the separately named 32K variant’s context.

modalities.note: Exact text API variant. The broader multimodal research model’s image input does not describe this alias.

reasoning.note: The sources discuss problem-solving and prompted reasoning, but do not explicitly establish a dedicated reasoning-mode flag for this exact alias. Clear the unsupported false value.

tool_call.note: Historical capability of the alias after its 0613 upgrade, explicitly announced twice. Today’s model table says unsupported and the API is shut down; retain the historical capability and disclose that conflict, without attributing it to the March 0314 snapshot.

description.value: Text-only GPT-4 API model with an 8,192-token context, later updated to the gpt-4-0613 snapshot.
description.note: Replace generic promotional task claims with the exact API variant, context and alias history.

patch.description: Text-only GPT-4 API model with an 8,192-token context, later updated to the gpt-4-0613 snapshot.

sources.label: Function calling and other API updates
Introducing Structured Outputs in the API

patch.notes: Historical gpt-4 text API alias, last pointing to gpt-4-0613. Initial public text access was March 14, 2023; image access described in the research launch was separate. Function calling was added with the June 2023 alias upgrade and is retained as historical capability despite today’s contradictory unsupported feature table. API access ended October 23, 2026. Transformer structure is documented; dense versus expert structure and parameter counts remain undisclosed. The dedicated reasoning flag is unverified.

summary: Confirm March 14, 2023 release, text-only 8,192-token API specifications and historical function calling of the 0613 alias target. Add verified Transformer architecture and proprietary classification, replace the generic description, and clear unsupported dedicated-reasoning=false. Total/active counts and dense-versus-expert subtype remain undisclosed after original-report and later first-party interpretability research checks. Record the current tool-support documentation conflict and October 23, 2026 shutdown.
